mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST) below 1,400k units signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < 1400 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods meeting the dual GDPC1/HOUST trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of four consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL above 2.5% and FEDFUNDS above 4.0% for two consecutive months signals a dual shock of inflation and restrictive policy, which increases uncertainty and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 2.5% AND FEDFUNDS > 4.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when both CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS > 4.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced consumption, which depresses demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average +10% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive months where RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average by more than 10%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their respective 12-month averages by more than 0.5% in the same month signals a broad-based labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average +0.5% AND UNRATE > 12-month moving average +0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during months when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 12-month moving averages by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between monthly HOUST and GDPC1 growth rates above 0.3% indicates synchronized expansion in housing and overall demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly HOUST and GDPC1 growth rates above 0.3% fails to predict positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns with statistical significance (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample tests.
